title: SQL schema description
description: The structure of a SQL database: its schemas, tables, columns, constraints, indexes, and the signatures of its programmable objects. Structure and signatures only -- no view, procedure, function or trigger body text appears anywhere in this format. The core is engine-neutral; anything that does not generalize lives in a per-engine `extensions` bag. Consumers must ignore properties they do not recognize. This $id is an identifier, not a fetchable URL.

schemaVersion.description: Semantic major version of this payload format, owned by hand and independent of the package versions. A consumer accepts a higher minor and rejects a higher major.

tool.title: ToolInfo
tool.description: The producer that wrote this document.

engine.title: SqlEngineInfo
engine.description: The database engine this document describes. Never null: a document with no engine cannot be read correctly.

name.description: The engine dialect. SQL Server is the only engine implemented; a reader must reject a dialect it does not know rather than guess.

version.description: Engine major version as a decimal string, e.g. '12' for Azure SQL Database, or null when the source does not report one.

targetPlatform.description: The platform the model targets, e.g. 'SqlAzure' or 'Sql160'. Normalized deliberately: the raw schema-provider string a project declares is a tooling implementation detail, not a fact about the database.

collation.description: Collation name, or null when the source carries only a locale identifier. A dacpac carries an LCID and comparison flags rather than a name, and this format does not guess at the mapping.

caseSensitive.description: Whether identifiers and string data compare case-sensitively under the model's collation. This is what governs identifier comparison across documents.

source.title: SqlSourceInfo
source.description: Where this document was read from. Carries no timestamp, deliberately: a document must be byte-identical when produced twice from the same input.

kind.description: What was read. Some fidelity differences are a function of this -- a project-sourced document can carry `sourceFile`, and expression text is comparable only between documents of the same kind.

schemas.description: Every user-defined schema, sorted by id. Empty when none.

tables.description: Every user-defined table, sorted by id. Empty when none.

views.description: Every user-defined view, sorted by id. Empty when none.

routines.description: Every user-defined procedure, function and aggregate, sorted by id. Empty when none.

sequences.description: Every user-defined sequence, sorted by id. Empty when none.

userDefinedTypes.description: Every user-defined type, sorted by id. Empty when none.

synonyms.description: Every synonym, sorted by id. Empty when none.

triggers.description: Every trigger, sorted by id. A trigger is top level because it is schema-named, and carries an explicit reference to the table it is attached to. Empty when none.

extensions.description: Per-engine facts that do not generalize, keyed by engine name. A consumer that ignores this entirely must still get a correct and complete structural picture: nothing here may change the meaning of a core member.

identifierPath.description: Identifier segments, verbatim and unquoted, in the model's own casing. This is the normative identity of an object; `id` is a derived rendering of it.

columnNames.description: Bare column names, resolved against the table the list appears under -- except inside a foreign key's `references`, where they resolve against the referenced table.

schema.title: SqlSchema
schema.description: A schema: the namespace objects are declared in.

description.description: Human description, or null when none is recorded. A dacpac carries this only as an extended property; prose authored as a SQL comment does not survive and arrives instead from an annotation sidecar.

table.title: SqlTable
table.description: A table, with its columns, constraints and indexes nested. Nested rather than top-level because a column cannot be named without naming its table.

columns.description: Columns in declared order. Ordinal is the array index and is not stored.

constraints.description: Every constraint on the table, including DEFAULT constraints, sorted by name with unnamed entries last in declared order.

indexes.description: Indexes that are not expressed as a constraint, sorted by name.

sourceFile.description: Repository-relative path of the file that declares this table. Present only when `source.kind` is 'project'; a dacpac flattens the file layout away.

column.title: SqlColumn
column.description: A column. Carries no derived flags: whether it is a key, a period boundary, or has a default are all facts of the table's constraints and temporal period, recorded once there. `dataType` is omitted when the source does not report one, which is the case for a computed column in a compiled model: the model records the expression and its dependencies but never resolves the resulting type.

nullable.description: Whether the column accepts NULL. Nullability lives here rather than on the data type, because the same type is nullable differently on a column, a parameter and a result column.

dataType.title: SqlDataType
dataType.description: A data type as the model resolves it, not as it was authored: DATETIME2 is recorded as datetime2(7) and DECIMAL(15) as decimal(15,0), because a compiled model cannot report what the author omitted.

name.description: The lowercase base type name, unqualified, e.g. 'varchar'. When `userDefined` is true this is instead the type's id, e.g. 'dbo.AccountNumber'.

userDefined.description: Changes how `name` is read. Required precisely so a consumer never has to guess.

length.description: Character or byte length. Omitted when the type takes none, and omitted when `maxLength` is true.

maxLength.description: True for varchar(max), nvarchar(max) and varbinary(max). A separate boolean rather than a sentinel length, because -1 is an engine internal and a string 'max' would not survive a typed model.

precision.description: Omitted when the type takes none.

scale.description: Omitted when the type takes none.

collation.description: Column-level collation override. Omitted when the column inherits the database collation. Not part of `rendered`.

rendered.description: The type written out, e.g. 'varchar(max)' or 'decimal(8,4)'. Derived, but stored, so that two producers cannot disagree about it. The algorithm is normative and given in the specification.

identity.title: SqlIdentity
identity.description: Presence of this member is what makes a column an identity column; there is no separate boolean.

seed.description: Decimal literal. A string because an identity on a BIGINT exceeds a 32-bit integer, and this format carries no 64-bit numeric type.

increment.description: Decimal literal, as a string, for the same reason as `seed`.

computedColumn.title: SqlComputedColumn
computedColumn.description: Presence of this member is what makes a column computed. The expression is kept because it belongs to the column's structural contract; a module body is not kept anywhere in this format.

expression.description: Opaque engine-normalized expression text. Comparable only between documents produced from the same `source.kind`.

constraint.title: SqlConstraint
constraint.description: A constraint of any kind, including DEFAULT. Defaults are modelled here rather than as a column member because they are named, and those names appear in deploy scripts and drift reports. `columns` holds the key columns in order for primaryKey, unique and foreignKey; the single defaulted column for default; and the columns the predicate names, possibly empty, for check.

name.description: The declared name, or null when the constraint is anonymous. A producer must not substitute an engine-generated name: those are assigned at deploy time and differ per database, which would make the document irreproducible.

expression.description: Present for check and default. Opaque engine-normalized text; see `computedColumn.expression`.

foreignKeyReference.title: SqlForeignKeyReference
foreignKeyReference.description: The target of a foreign key. Its `columns` are bare names in the referenced table, paired positionally with the constraint's own `columns`.

index.title: SqlIndex
index.description: An index. Physical storage choices -- clustering, fill factor, compression -- are engine-specific and live in `extensions` rather than here. `includedColumns` holds non-key columns carried in the leaf level, and is omitted when empty.

filter.description: Predicate of a filtered or partial index. Omitted when the index covers every row.

indexColumn.title: SqlIndexColumn
indexColumn.description: A key column of an index, in index order.

descending.description: Sort direction, when the source reports one. Omitted when it does not: a compiled model does not carry index sort direction, so a producer reading one leaves this absent rather than asserting ascending.

temporal.title: SqlTemporal
temporal.description: The table's period. Presence of this member is what makes a table temporal, and a history table is identified only by another table naming it here -- one fact, recorded in one place.

historyTable.description: Id of the history table, or null for an application-time period, which has none.

view.title: SqlView
view.description: A view's signature. The defining SELECT is never recorded.

columns.description: Resolved result columns. Null means the producer could not resolve them -- a SELECT * over something outside the model -- and is distinct from an empty array, which means there are none.

routine.title: SqlRoutine
routine.description: A procedure, function or aggregate, as a signature. The body is never recorded. `returns` is present only for a scalar function.

resultColumns.description: Result columns of a table-valued function. Always empty for a procedure: a procedure's result set is not part of any compiled model, at any fidelity.

name.description: The canonical token with its prefix, e.g. '@StoreNumber'.

defaultExpression.description: Presence of this member is what gives the parameter a default.

sequence.title: SqlSequence
sequence.description: A sequence. Its current value is runtime state, not structure, and is deliberately absent.

startValue.description: Decimal literal, as a string: a sequence bound exceeds a 32-bit integer.

cacheSize.description: Omitted when caching is on but the engine chooses the size.

userDefinedType.title: SqlUserDefinedType
userDefinedType.description: A user-defined type. A table type reuses the table's own column and constraint definitions, deliberately: a table type is a table shape, and a second set of definitions would drift from the first. `dataType` and `nullable` are present only when `kind` is 'alias'; `columns` and `constraints` only when it is 'table'. Presence carries applicability here because a `$ref` cannot be made nullable without sibling keys, which would fork a duplicate type in one language and be ignored in the other.

target.description: The target name exactly as written, which may be multi-part and may name a remote server.

targetPath.description: The target parsed into segments, or null when the target lies outside the model and cannot be resolved.

trigger.title: SqlTrigger
trigger.description: A trigger's declaration. The body is never recorded.

table.description: Id of the table the trigger is attached to, or null for a DDL trigger.

events.description: For a DML trigger: insert, update, delete. For a DDL trigger: the DDL event names.

annotations.title: SqlAnnotations
annotations.description: The annotation sidecar: prose a compiled model cannot carry. Reachable from nothing in the payload -- it is a separate document a producer is handed, and it is defined here so the type is generated in both languages from one source rather than hand-written twice.

descriptions.description: Maps an object address to its description. The address is an object's id for a top-level object, and '<owner id>.<name>' for a nested column, constraint, index or parameter. A key matching nothing in the document is an error: a stale annotation naming a dropped column is the failure this file exists to prevent.
